headline: Bad loans again exceed Tk 6 lakh crore in Bangladesh's banking sector, reaching 32.78% of total disbursed loans
summary: Despite numerous policy support measures for defaulted borrowers, the country's banking sector sees bad loans surge past Tk 6 lakh crore, highlighting its fragile state.
details: Bangladesh's banking sector is facing a significant challenge as bad loans have once again surpassed Tk 6 lakh crore. As of the end of June, defaulted loans stood at Tk 6,06,555 crore, representing 32.78 percent of the total disbursed loans.
This marks a substantial increase of Tk 17,851 crore in defaulted loans over the last three months alone. The bad loan ratio previously stood at 32.26 percent, indicating a continuous upward trend.

The banking sector previously saw defaulted loans peak at Tk 6.44 lakh crore, or nearly 36 percent of disbursed loans, at the end of September 2025. A sharp jump in bad loans occurred after the fall of the Awami League-led government in August 2024, with businesses linked to the previous administration defaulting heavily.

Both the interim government and the BNP-led government have implemented various initiatives to curb the rise in bad loans. These measures include easier loan rescheduling policies, a one-time exit policy, and other support mechanisms.

However, these initiatives have largely proven ineffective. Bangladesh Bank Spokesman Arief Hossain Khan noted that many borrowers cannot afford the required down payments for rescheduling, and interest continues to accumulate, adding to the defaulted sums.

The fragile state of the sector led the government to merge five crisis-hit banks: EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, and Union Bank. These banks, except EXIM Bank, were largely dominated by the controversial S Alam Group and have now been merged into a state-run Shariah-based bank.

A chief executive of a private bank stated that a significant portion of the high defaulted loans stems from large, government-linked borrowers from the previous regime who are no longer in business. This has made loan recovery particularly challenging for banks.

To address this, bankers suggest borrower-specific measures, such as settling overdue loans for a reduced amount rather than demanding the full sum inflated by accumulated interest. They also propose offering repayment time alongside interest waivers for the one-time exit policy to be more effective.

Experts attribute the persistent issue to widespread irregularities, scams, and weak oversight within the financial sector in previous years. Tareq Refat Ullah Khan, managing director of BRAC Bank, emphasized the need for proactive, pragmatic, and sometimes unconventional approaches to loan recovery.

Zahid Hussain, former lead economist at the World Bank’s Dhaka office, warned that repeated regulatory forbearance for defaulters has sent a wrong signal, encouraging borrowers to expect extensions. He stressed that authorities must change this approach to prevent further damage to the banking sector.

headline_marked: [[Bus driver Majed needs urgent financial aid]] for abdominal cancer treatment
headline: Bus driver Majed needs urgent financial aid for abdominal cancer treatment
summary: Majedul Islam, a 48-year-old bus driver and sole earner for his family, has been diagnosed with abdominal cancer. His treatment requires an estimated BDT 5-6 lakh, pushing his family into severe financial crisis.
details: Md. Majedul Islam, 48, a resident of Keranipara in Tushbhandar, Lalmonirhat Sadar Upazila, has recently been diagnosed with abdominal cancer. His family has been informed by doctors that his initial treatment will require an estimated BDT 5-6 lakh.

Majedul, an irregular long-distance bus driver, is the sole breadwinner for his family, which includes his wife, a ninth-grade daughter, and a three-year-old son. Due to his illness, he is unable to work regularly, leading to extreme financial hardship for the family.

The family is struggling to cover both food and medical expenses. In this dire situation, Majedul Islam has appealed to affluent individuals, organizations, and kind-hearted people across the country for financial assistance.

Those wishing to help can send money via bKash/Nagad to 01820273487 and 01752998972. Bank transfers can be made to account holder M.U. Ahmed, account number 4405734084093, Sonali Bank, Dhaka University Campus Branch.
